analysis:
The only change is in .github/workflows/ci.yml. The single test-provider lane of 5 Macs is split into five lanes, test-provider-1 through test-provider-5 (head lines 43-47), each requesting 1 runner. The test-provider job now selects its runner with fromJSON(routes)[format('test-provider-{0}', matrix.shard)] (head line 143). Permissions are unchanged: the route job keeps `permissions: {}` and the workflow keeps `contents: read`. No new secrets, triggers or untrusted-input interpolation are added. The format() argument comes from the static matrix [1..5], not from user-controlled data, so it creates no injection vector.

I looked for a security regression through runner routing and found none. The darkbloom-route.yml routing logic is outside the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that the per-shard lane names are accepted or that it falls back to the Blacksmith runner. A missing key would cause a CI failure or availability problem, not a confidentiality or integrity regression. The provider-test-gate still requires test-provider and test-provider-summary to succeed whenever provider files changed, so test coverage enforcement is unchanged. A pull request could in principle run on a Darkbloom Sandbox runner as before; this PR does not alter the trust placement of those runners.

The change touches no provider runtime, attestation, key or cache code, so the retained threat IDs (including T-041) are not affected. The unverified items are the route workflow's handling of the new lane names and the sandbox runner isolation. Neither was shown to be a defect in this diff.
